hypothesis: Hypothesis 4 (beyond the original V3 candidates): Economic Calendar Event Volatility
research_question: Does price action around scheduled high-impact economic releases show a statistically meaningful, tradeable volatility expansion that persists after realistic spread/transaction costs, regardless of direction?

event_data_source.description: Hand-curated table built from official, read-only, government/central-bank archives (not the project's own approximate econ_calendar.py, which is explicitly a rough weekly-window heuristic unsuitable for this test)
sources: federalreserve.gov FOMC meeting calendar (main page + fomchistorical2020.htm)
bls.gov year-by-year release schedule archives (/schedule/{year}/home.htm) for NFP and CPI

round_1_statistical_volatility_expansion.description: Pure statistics: realized vol (event windows vs. control), breakout-beyond-range incidence, sample cost-adjusted proxy. M15, EUR_USD & GBP_USD, 1h pre-event / 30min+2h post-event windows.

realized_volatility.stable_by_year_2020_2024: ratio 3.5-6.2x every year, never close to control's ~2.4x
realized_volatility.interpretation: Real, large, overwhelmingly robust effect - the strongest raw statistical finding across the entire V3+V4 search (14 hypotheses prior to this one)

breakout_incidence_0.5xATR.interpretation: Statistically distinguishable but the 0.5xATR threshold was poorly calibrated - near-ceiling for BOTH event and control groups, a weaker/less informative measure than the raw volatility comparison

cost_adjusted_edge_ex_post_direction.caveat: Direction chosen with hindsight (known eventual breakout side, not a real-time rule) - this number could not establish real-time tradeability, only that the magnitude of the move clears realistic mid-window Bid/Ask cost when direction happens to be known in advance

spread_resolution_check.description: Targeted check: can M15-resolution cached data see the true execution cost at the instant of release? Compares each event bar's own Bid/Ask Open (all 125 events land exactly on M15 boundaries) against the prior bar's close-based spread, and against that bar's own realized intrabar range.
spread_resolution_check.interpretation: Open-based spread shows NO widening at all (ratio ~1.0-1.02, indistinguishable from normal quiet-market spread), while the bar's own realized range is 10-15x larger. Decisive evidence that a genuine spread spike lasting seconds is averaged away between 15-minute checkpoints - M15 resolution cannot reliably capture true execution cost at the moment of a news-driven break.

round_2_breakout_trigger_simulation.description: Genuine non-lookahead, mechanical, dual-sided OCO breakout-trigger simulation. Standalone (not routed through backtest_engine.run_backtest(), whose signal-at-T/fill-at-T+1-Open convention doesn't match 'enter the instant broken'); backtest_engine.py and risk_management.py untouched. Fixed design, nothing swept: 0.1xATR entry buffer (reused from signals_london_sweep_m15.py), structural stop at opposite range side (same buffer style), 1:1 R:R target (same value as V1/V2), 2h trigger window, 24h max hold, same-bar-both-triggered excluded, R-multiple outcome measure (no position sizing/dollar P&L).

execution_cost_scenarios.optimistic: fill = trigger +/- that bar's own realized average spread
execution_cost_scenarios.conservative: optimistic +/- 0.25x that bar's own (Ask_High-Bid_Low), applied only when the trigger fires on the first bar after the event (177/184 = 96% of triggers did)

round_2_breakout_trigger_simulation.interpretation: The optimistic scenario is the strongest raw signal in the whole search (large, highly significant, consistent across both instruments and all three event types). Under the conservative scenario - a modest, formulaic, non-tuned adjustment applied to 96% of the trade sample, since that's where almost every trigger lands - the entire edge collapses to statistically indistinguishable from zero, FOMC and NFP individually flip to non-significant negative, and the year-by-year pattern becomes genuinely inconsistent (2020-2022 lean negative, only 2023-2024 hold up). This is exactly the pre-committed 'sign/significance inconsistent across years' rejection trigger, firing under the scenario that matters.

pre_committed_rejection_criteria_evaluat.mean_r_not_significantly_positive_optimi: NOT triggered - optimistic is strongly, significantly positive
pre_committed_rejection_criteria_evaluat.optimistic_positive_but_conservative_sig: NOT triggered by strict letter (conservative is negative but p=0.73, not significant) - but see next criterion
pre_committed_rejection_criteria_evaluat.sign_or_significance_inconsistent_across: TRIGGERED under the conservative scenario - 2020-2022 lean negative, 2023-2024 positive; FOMC and NFP flip negative individually
pre_committed_rejection_criteria_evaluat.trigger_sample_too_small: NOT the binding constraint - 179 non-forced trades, above the 150 convention

round_1_2_verdict_superseded_by_round_3: REJECTED, but not cleanly - the market phenomenon (large, robust volatility expansion) was confirmed real, but tradeability could not be determined because M15-resolution data was shown unable to measure true execution cost at the moment of a break. Resolving this required finer data - see round_3 below, which now supersedes this as the final, decisive answer.

round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.description: Reruns round 2's exact fixed design (0.1xATR entry buffer, structural stop opposite range side same buffer style, 1:1 R:R target, 24h max hold, dual-sided OCO, no-hindsight walk-forward - nothing changed or tuned) but now driven by S5 (5-second) candles - confirmed empirically the finest granularity OANDA's API offers, available back to the start of DEVELOPMENT for both EUR_USD and GBP_USD via the same existing read-only connection. Fetched as ~310 targeted event windows (not a bulk continuous download). Entry fill = realistic Ask_High(long)/Bid_Low(short) of the triggering S5 bar, worsened by SLIPPAGE_ATR_FRACTION=0.02xATR reused verbatim from backtest_engine.py. Stop/target monitored via S5 through the 2h post-event window, falling back to existing cached M15 data from 2h to the 24h max hold. Standalone simulation, backtest_engine.py/risk_management.py/live connector all untouched.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.data_resolution_determination: S5 (5-second) confirmed the minimum/finest resolution needed and available - directly resolves round 2's open question. Verified empirically (not assumed) for both instruments across the full DEVELOPMENT window before use.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.chronological_split: dataset_split.py's existing three-way split reused unchanged: DEVELOPMENT = train (125 events, walk-forward by year), VALIDATION = genuine out-of-sample checked exactly once (31 new events for 2024-07-15 to 2025-07-15, hand-curated from the same official Fed/BLS sources). FINAL_RESERVED NOT accessed.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.ambiguous_same_bar_rate: Dropped from 26.4% (M15, round 2) to 5.2% (13/250, S5, round 3) - confirms finer resolution resolves almost all of round 2's entry ambiguity.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.trigger_lag: Median 0 seconds, mean 108.5 seconds (right-skewed) - most triggers fire on the very first S5 tick after the event.

results.by_session_utc_hour: Every UTC-hour bucket (12, 13, 18, 19 - the two fixed event-time clusters) is flat-to-negative in both DEVELOPMENT and VALIDATION; no session shows a real edge.

round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.interpretation: Negative expectancy every year in DEVELOPMENT (trending toward breakeven late, but never positive) - and that improving trend did NOT continue into VALIDATION, which reversed sharply back to -0.585R, more unprofitable than DEVELOPMENT as a whole. Confirms round 2's core concern directly: the earlier 'optimistic' M15 result (+0.352R) was an artifact of underestimated execution cost. Real S5 bid/ask plus realistic slippage doesn't just erase the edge, it flips it solidly negative and keeps it negative out-of-sample.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.pre_committed_rejection_rule_applied: 'If H4 does not remain profitable out-of-sample after costs, reject it.' VALIDATION expectancy is significantly negative (p<0.0001) - rule triggered, hypothesis rejected.
round_3_s5_finest_resolution_breakout_tr.data: hypothesis_tests/data/economic_events_validation.csv (VALIDATION event table, new); hypothesis_tests/data/s5_cache/ (raw S5 candle cache, NOT committed - regenerable via the fetch script, see .gitignore)

verdict: REJECTED - decisively and cleanly, resolving the earlier data-resolution-limited finding into a confident answer. At the finest resolution OANDA's API offers (S5), with realistic bid/ask fills and slippage, the breakout-trigger strategy is unprofitable in DEVELOPMENT (expectancy -0.213R, p=0.0012, PF=0.649) and MORE unprofitable out-of-sample in VALIDATION (expectancy -0.585R, p<0.0001, PF=0.262) - consistent across both instruments individually, all three event types, and nearly every session bucket. The underlying volatility-expansion phenomenon (round 1) was never in doubt and remains a genuine market fact; what round 3 resolves is that it is NOT capturable as a tradeable edge once realistic execution is modeled at adequate resolution. Per the user's own pre-committed rule ('if H4 does not remain profitable out-of-sample after costs, reject it'), this hypothesis is rejected. Does not proceed to a demo-bot validation stage, since that step was explicitly conditional on survival.
does_not_proceed_to: V4 strategy build or demo-bot validation stage - the phenomenon is real but not tradeable at any resolution this project has been able to test, including the finest OANDA offers.
note_for_future_work: This lead is now closed, not merely paused - round 3 answered the question round 2 left open, with a confident, out-of-sample-confirmed rejection. No further work on this specific hypothesis is warranted absent a fundamentally different execution model (e.g. limit rather than stop-style entries) or a different market/instrument where spread dynamics differ materially.
